svg.title: Instance settings in the app, not only in environment variables — SoftTrack web design mockup (#310)
svg.desc: Everything about an instance is an environment variable read once at startup, so closing registration takes a shell and a restart. A settings page for site admins holds the instance’s name, registration, the landing page, how long links last, the largest attachment, defaults and SMTP; a value set in the environment wins and is shown as locked; secrets are written and never read back.
svg.text: Instance settings in the app, not only in environment variables

g.text: Administration → Settings, signed in as a site admin
What this SoftTrack is called and how it behaves. Applied without a restart.
Shown in the browser tab and in emails.
Anybody who reaches the sign-in page can make an account.
What somebody who is signed out sees first.
Links to choose a password last as long.
Each person can choose their own, #315.
Stored in the database, so every worker reads the same value.
The page shows that a password is set, and not the password.
The same for the single sign-on secret.

svg.text: What stays out of the page
Changing those from a web page would be a way to lock everybody
out. No settings per team here, no theming and no custom CSS.
Done when Administration → Settings holds the name, open registration, the landing page, invitation and reset lifetimes, the largest attachment, the default language and
timezone, who may create teams and SMTP with a test button; a setting set in the environment is shown and cannot be changed; secrets are never read back; values are stored in
the database and applied without a restart; the database address, SECRET_KEY and attachment storage stay in the environment; and every change is recorded.
